hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds leads Florida GOP governor's race with $90 million raised as rival challenges eligibility of third candidate
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds strengthened his position in the Republican primary for Florida governor, announcing that his campaign and affiliated political committee have raised more than $90 million this cycle, with more than $23 million coming in the second quarter alone. The campaign recently launched a $20 million statewide advertising buy as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds, viewed as the front-runner to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis, secured endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by DeSantis. He also has the backing of the two incoming legislative leaders, Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison. These endorsements carry particular weight in a primary where DeSantis himself has not endorsed a successor, though several figures from his administration have begun supporting Donalds.

The race took a contentious turn when Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit seeking to remove Republican candidate James Fishback from the ballot. Collins argues that Fishback does not meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before being elected. The legal complaint points to Fishback's ties to Washington, D.C., including allegations that he claimed a D.C. property as a primary residence and voted there in 2020. "Election integrity matters," Collins said in explaining the challenge. Fishback has denied being ineligible, arguing he was born and raised in Florida. He accused Collins of attempting to damage his campaign and suggested, without providing evidence, that Collins is working with Donalds. At a news conference, Fishback announced, "The first motion we will file is for Congressman Donalds and Jay Collins to release all communications between their two campaigns."

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for Facebook comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended after writing comments that labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi.

In the Thursday filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate. However, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, and it's unclear when a final decision will be made.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis moves to designate CAIR, Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa as terrorist groups under new Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations and other organizations under a new state law that took effect July 1.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis moved this week to use a new state law that gives Florida a process to designate organizations as terrorist groups. The law, which took effect July 1, allows the governor and Florida Cabinet to designate organizations based on recommendations from state domestic security officials. DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations, including cartel-linked groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

If approved by the Cabinet, the designations could block taxpayer funding, contracts or other public support for listed groups. The law also creates penalties for providing material support and could subject some organizations to dissolution under state statute. CAIR and civil-rights groups quickly sued in federal court, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it could threaten the organizations' ability to operate in Florida. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, said the designation process violates free-speech and due-process rights because "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound man loses fiancée in deadly home fire, community launches fundraiser
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is receiving support from his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire earlier this week.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire earlier this week. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke exclusively about the loss. She learned of White's death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. Fenn described the scene as "completely a state of devastation." She reflected on White's character, noting she was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing the piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday is July 4, meaning she passed just days before turning 47. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby for Fourth of July boating traffic
cards.teaser: Hundreds of boaters are hitting Martin County waterways for the Fourth of July weekend. Maritime Response Unit teams will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south of the county.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida's waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will have two boats with medics on standby positioned in the north and south of Martin County to assist anyone in need. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched off the ramps Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy, said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry encouraged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents push for fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as budget talks loom
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. The dispute will be taken up during budget discussions on July 15.
hero.body:
A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating friction between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with potential repairs that could cost the town significant money. The Colony Condos residents say people accessing the public walkway are crossing through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now marking the boundary between the public path and private land, residents have seen an increase in unwanted foot traffic and parking violations during peak summer months.

Lori Hill, who lives at the Colony Condos, described the recurring problem of visitors using the area. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. She explained that people push through the bushes with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs, then stay for extended periods. The residents have had to call police multiple times to address trespassers. Hill noted that when residents previously tried to confront visitors, they often received rude responses. Before the fence was removed, the physical barrier made the property line clear and prevented these intrusions.

Not all beachgoers share the same perspective on the situation. Michael House, a visitor to the area, said he walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot and has not observed the problems residents describe. He pointed out that adequate free parking exists nearby and suggested that property damage or littering, rather than simple property line crossings, should be the primary concern.

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials clarified that the town is not legally required to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern expressed interest in exploring lower-cost alternatives to a traditional fence. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Hill said residents hope the town will act to address their concerns. The council decided to consider the fence replacement during its upcoming budget discussions scheduled for July 15, when town officials will weigh the costs and merits of reinstalling a barrier at the beach access point.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, receiving "A" or "B" ratings. S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic jump from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year, becoming one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating. The others include Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary. School grades are based on factors including student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework.

Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround effort. Three years ago, staff began taking a closer look at the foundation of student learning by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, which contributed to the renewed A rating. The district's overall success is reflected in its record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year as ground beef and strawberry prices climb
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation. Ground beef is up 5.5% and strawberries are up 12.4% after a Florida frost.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased prices. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices have also climbed, up 5.3% compared to last year.

Not all items on the Fourth of July cookout menu carry higher price tags. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades is available at competitive prices. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals and creating a meal plan to reduce food waste as strategies for managing cookout expenses.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied reconstruction coverage by Anthem Blue Cross hours before surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance company deny coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Her surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, is calling for policy changes on GalaFlex mesh treatment.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives her patients the least amount of complications. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem stated it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that without FDA approval, the mesh does not meet its medical policy standards. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial. Meanwhile, a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act, a federal law designed to protect breast cancer patients from being denied treatments.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall at 10:30 a.m.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing the entire state of Florida. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing for millions of viewers, but expressed confidence the band will rise to the occasion. She explained the physical demands of marching band, noting students must simultaneously play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on marching precision and timing, knowing everyone will see what the Boca High band can do. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone said she has full confidence her students will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it showcases how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation doubling slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for renovations projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will expand the dock from 18 to 44 slips.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a purpose beyond capacity expansion. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said this solution will enable the company to continue boarding people during construction.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to FDOT to assist with a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike. The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is underway.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there's a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city, describing it as a way to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated guideway connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to the airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, as well as nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected for pedestrians or travelers. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost a small fraction of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources could include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. The award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and local government, and creating opportunities for residents to shape the city's future. Miller-Anderson noted that the recognition reinforces the city's momentum. "Winning this brings back community pride," she said. City officials believe the designation celebrates progress already made while positioning the community for future opportunities and growth.

The recognition sends a message that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and where residents remain actively involved in shaping their community's direction. The other nine cities receiving the 2026 award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. The land transfer will assist FDOT in constructing the interchange as part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city, and the interchange is designed to improve accessibility while keeping up with growth.

FDOT crews are currently working on the first phase of the Midway Road Widening Project, expanding the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike is also still in the design phase. FDOT is working on improving the Turnpike bridge in addition to the partial interchange. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City Council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her and her fiancé Mark's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who has been friends with White for eight years, spoke about the loss after returning to the scene in the days following the tragedy. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing the piano, kids and people, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his one and only child Jacob tragically. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak because her birthday is July 4, meaning she passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% from last year, ground beef and buns see biggest increases
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a Fourth of July meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the largest increase at 12.4%, and ice cream prices are up 5.3%.

Not all items have become more expensive. Potato prices have declined this year, providing savings for those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can offer competitive pricing. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals for items on your shopping list. She emphasized that the most significant way families can manage costs is by reducing food waste, which starts with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Hundreds of boaters are hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend, and Martin County Maritime Response Unit is preparing with two boats staffed with medics on standby.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will deploy two boats with medics positioned in the north and south parts of Martin County to assist anyone needing help, whether it's a minor injury like a stubbed toe or serious emergencies including cardiac issues and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, said safety is their top priority on the water. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and had a double bilateral mastectomy, but her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for reconstruction less than 24 hours before the scheduled procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to undergo a double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery was scheduled, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh, is still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body and popular among plastic surgeons, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, argues insurance companies should reconsider their stance. She uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients, stating the product produces fewer complications than other options. Billington has publicly criticized insurance denials on social media. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and Matthew Apthorp shared patients' denial stories, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex over a week ago. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial while a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health & Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: California transit company proposes elevated self-driving network linking West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would link the airport to the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger described the concept as functioning like a "horizontal elevator," designed to bypass traffic congestion entirely while making no intermediate stops.

Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected. He cited increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road as evidence the region needs new transportation solutions. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which previous South Florida discussions estimated at $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is working hard during the summer months as they prepare for a state title push in the 2026 fall season. Last year, the team finished with a 10-2 record and won the district championship, but a second-round playoff loss has motivated them to achieve even more this year. The players and coaching staff believe they can go further in the postseason than they did in their previous campaign.

Head football coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class, noting that most of them have been with the program since middle school. This experience and continuity has given the team stability and success throughout their years at Saint Andrew's. Robertson expressed optimism about the senior class's final year, saying "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had." Because of this veteran leadership, the program made the decision to schedule more difficult opponents this fall to challenge themselves and attract attention to the program.

Senior Jack Williams explained the team's reasoning for taking on tougher competition. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that advancing in the playoffs matters more than winning every regular season game. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters."

The team is using summer workouts as preparation and motivation for the upcoming season. Senior Edmyer St. Jean reflected on how the daily training sessions provide purpose as the team works toward their goals. "It just adds up every day as something like to look forward to. Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record." The Scots are committed to the demanding summer program as they aim to have their best season in program history while competing for a state championship.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams are on standby with medics as hundreds of boaters hit the waterways for the Fourth of July holiday weekend.

Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will deploy two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County to assist boaters. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy, are taking extra precautions on the water. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver who won't drink, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk social media post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court document Thursday opposing a judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended after controversial Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended last year after making social media comments that labeled Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation to reinstate Theobald, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contended that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling in her order last month, which stated that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his job, with no decision date announced.

cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is receiving community support after his fiance died Monday in a home fire that preliminary findings suggest was caused by an electrical issue.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran's roof lien removed and repairs completed after WPTV investigates contractor
cards.teaser: A disabled Lantana veteran got his roof repaired and a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home within hours after WPTV contacted the roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said they left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails beginning in January. When he attempted to follow up, including visiting the company's building two or three times, he received no response except for one worker's promise on Feb. 5 that the owner would call him, which never happened.

Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien on McCoy's property, stating the company furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for his work but was not paid. When WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the roofing company's owner about the unpaid materials and lien, he declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour of that conversation, Gulfeagle Supply signed and notarized a final waiver of lien, removing the lien from McCoy's home. The contractor also sent crews back to fix the two unfinished areas on the roof, completing the work about two hours after McCoy received the waiver.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Florida Turnpike interchange and Midway Road expansion
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to FDOT for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with a partial Florida Turnpike interchange and the Midway Road Widening Project. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land to FDOT at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Tee Box virtual golf center near Delray Beach delayed three months and $90,000 after contractor issues
cards.teaser: A virtual golf training center preparing to open on Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard near Delray Beach faced three-month delays and $90,000 in costs after contractor problems forced complete rework.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said his business was delayed from an April opening to July after the licensed contractor hired to prepare the space constantly pushed off work. The work ultimately had to be redone, creating costly setbacks that Molen estimates at $90,000, not including lost revenue or the expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. Molen said the issues resulted in double payment for electricians, HVAC work and drywall.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues affect 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify contractors have proper licenses and insurance before any work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is moving forward and putting the problems behind him. Tee Box is set to open July 17.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds leads Florida GOP governor's race with $90 million raised as rival challenges eligibility of third candidate
hero.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds strengthened his position in the Republican primary for Florida governor, announcing that his campaign and affiliated political committee have raised more than $90 million this cycle, with more than $23 million coming in the second quarter alone. The campaign recently launched a $20 million statewide advertising buy as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds, viewed as the front-runner to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis, secured endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by DeSantis. He also has the backing of the two incoming legislative leaders, Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison. These endorsements carry particular weight in a primary where DeSantis himself has not endorsed a successor, though several figures from his administration have begun supporting Donalds.

The race took a contentious turn when Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit seeking to remove Republican candidate James Fishback from the ballot. Collins argues that Fishback does not meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before being elected. The legal complaint points to Fishback's ties to Washington, D.C., including allegations that he claimed a D.C. property as a primary residence and voted there in 2020. "Election integrity matters," Collins said in explaining the challenge. Fishback has denied being ineligible, arguing he was born and raised in Florida. He accused Collins of attempting to damage his campaign and suggested, without providing evidence, that Collins is working with Donalds. At a news conference, Fishback announced, "The first motion we will file is for Congressman Donalds and Jay Collins to release all communications between their two campaigns."

Gov. DeSantis moved to use a new state law allowing Florida to designate organizations as terrorist groups. The law, which took effect July 1, allows the governor and Florida Cabinet to designate organizations based on recommendations from state domestic security officials. DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood, and Antifa, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations. If approved by the Cabinet, the designations could block taxpayer funding, contracts, and public support for listed groups and create penalties for providing material support. CAIR and civil-rights groups quickly sued in federal court, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it could threaten the organizations' ability to operate in Florida.

Florida also advanced restrictions on undocumented students. The State Board of Education voted to move forward with rules barring undocumented students from Florida's 28 state colleges and adult education programs, including GED preparation courses. The state university system's Board of Governors separately advanced a plan barring undocumented students from enrolling at Florida's more competitive public universities beginning with the 2027-28 academic year, though currently enrolled students would not be affected. Supporters argue taxpayer-backed institutions should serve only lawfully present students. Immigrant advocates pushed back, with student Alexander Vallejos saying, "We're just asking for an opportunity to earn our future through education."

cards.headline: Former DeSantis aides accuse Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous social media accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple X accounts were deactivated after allegations they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, who is running for governor.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. The accusations came from prominent veterans of Gov. Ron DeSantis' communications team, including Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to one known to be used by Layla Collins. Screenshots verified this connection through two-factor authentication. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of posts promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor.

Redfern joined the criticism, stating the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. After Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly, both accounts were deactivated. Both Pushaw and Redfern have previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. DeSantis has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race and cannot seek a third term because of term limits.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site with housing, museum and 13-acre park
cards.teaser: The Burg Bid proposal would transform acres of stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district centered around Samuel Davis Park and The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the city's preferred path forward for redeveloping Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the proposal outlines an $8.1 billion plan to transform stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, workforce training, public art and entertainment space. The team proposes purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, valuing the full land package at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be due when a purchase and sale agreement is executed.

Unlike the previous redevelopment deal centered on a new stadium, The Burg Bid organizes around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central park serving as a civic and cultural space. The park will include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, splash pad, café areas and a concert lawn, as part of 18.5 acres of total public park space. The proposal also calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over 15 years, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. Blue Sky Communities serves as the affordable housing partner. Development would occur in three phases lasting about five years each, with the team's lease ending after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: Florida Secretary of State asks court to keep Paula Stark off ballot after filing deadline mishap
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the courts to keep Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork less than 30 minutes before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the courts to keep Paula Stark off the ballot, casting doubt on her claims about a paperwork mix-up that disqualified her candidacy. Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12. Five state employees gave sworn written court declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the crucial Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, nor was he accidentally handed it back when submitting other paperwork. Byrd argued in his response that had Stark or Davis exercised care by questioning why Form 6 was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Davis was at the Division.

Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said three weeks after the deadline, Stark still hadn't submitted Form 6. Reeve noted Stark was one of 12 candidates who didn't properly turn in the form; half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve documented Stark's history of paperwork issues, including a campaign finance report filed over one month late, excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. Audits found inconsistent transfers between campaign and office accounts in the 2022 and 2024 cycles. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines.

cards.headline: Florida State Board of Education advances ban on undocumented students at state colleges and adult education programs
cards.teaser: The State Board of Education voted to bar undocumented students from Florida's 28 state colleges and adult education programs, including GED preparation courses.
cards.body:
The State Board of Education voted to move forward with rules that would bar undocumented students from Florida's 28 state colleges and adult education programs, including GED preparation courses that can serve as a bridge to college or workforce training. This action follows a separate move by the state university system's Board of Governors, which has advanced a plan to bar undocumented students from enrolling at Florida's more competitive public universities beginning with the 2027-28 academic year. Currently enrolled students would not be affected under that university proposal.

Supporters of the restrictions argue taxpayer-backed institutions should be reserved for students who are lawfully present in the United States. Immigrant advocates and students pushed back, saying the rules would close doors for young people who grew up in Florida and graduated from Florida schools. Alexander Vallejos, a student Dreamer, said they are just asking for an opportunity to earn their future through education, adding that when Dreamers succeed, Florida succeeds. The moves come after Florida previously eliminated in-state tuition rates for many undocumented students, including some protected under DACA.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis moves to designate CAIR, Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa as terrorist groups under new Florida law
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations and other organizations under a new state law that took effect July 1.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis moved this week to use a new state law that gives Florida a process to designate organizations as terrorist groups. The law, which took effect July 1, allows the governor and Florida Cabinet to designate organizations based on recommendations from state domestic security officials. DeSantis said Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood and Antifa, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations, including cartel-linked groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

If approved by the Cabinet, the designations could block taxpayer funding, contracts or other public support for listed groups. The law also creates penalties for providing material support and could subject some organizations to dissolution under state statute. CAIR and civil-rights groups quickly sued in federal court, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it could threaten the organizations' ability to operate in Florida. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, said the designation process violates free-speech and due-process rights because "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review."

cards.headline: Attorney General Uthmeier and CFO Ingoglia endorse Byron Donalds for Florida governor
cards.teaser: Donalds picked up endorsements from two statewide officials appointed by DeSantis as he builds institutional support in the Republican primary.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, friends rally to support surviving fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiance. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
hero.body:

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year over controversial social media comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, faced suspension following Facebook comments that labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him from his position was appropriate.

Livingstone issued her order last month citing a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald gets his job back. Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as ground beef and strawberry prices climb
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout comes with a higher price tag this year as inflation drives up the cost of key ingredients. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Ground beef is up 5.5%, buns are up 7.7%, and strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting potato chip and salad shoppers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shoppers compare stores to find the best deals, cut down on food waste and start with a meal plan to keep costs in check.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an 'A' rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. According to district leaders, 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the most significant success stories came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which jumped from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround effort. The school had narrowly missed a "B" rating the previous year. Three years ago, staff modified the school's early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 through kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for her reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health."

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become a controversial treatment for breast reconstruction. While approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications. Despite her insurer's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to Billington. Last year, after investigative reporting, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.
